name: cbc-01-cxx-reference-baseline
title: C++ ground-truth baseline
claim:
Built the authors' C++ project against chaste/release on the mini and generated the
ground-truth cell-sorting baseline for all five models to t=100. Reduced to fractional
boundary length, it qualitatively reproduces the paper's Fig 3: VT stalls highest, OS
sorts most, CP engulfs. This is the reference cbc-04 diffs against.

findings.summary:
All five models ran to completion (rc=0) and produced fractional-length trajectories that
qualitatively match paper Fig 3 (k_pert=1). Normalizing by the value at labelling (t=10),
as Fig 3 does: OS 0.08, CP 0.19, CA 0.50, VM 0.55, VT 0.91.
findings.evidence:
cxx-baseline/CellSorting/{Ca,Potts,Node,Mesh,Vertex}/results_from_time_{0,10}/
heterotypicboundary.dat, reduced by pbg_chaste.sorting_analysis into
cxx-baseline/fractional_length_by_model.csv. Raw endpoints at t=110:
CA 0.461->0.231, CP 0.524->0.097, OS 0.480->0.039, VT 0.485->0.440, VM 0.494->0.271.
Ordering (VT stalls highest, OS lowest, CP low) matches the paper's Fig 3-left black curves.
findings.interpretation:
The authors' own code is the ground truth by construction; this confirms our build + the
paper-parameter restoration are correct. The paper's "OS/VT differ from CA/CP/VM" claim
shows up as VT plateauing near its start (0.91 normalized) while CP/OS drive the interface
down. OS reaching the lowest value is consistent with the paper's note that OS/VT fully
SEPARATE (rather than engulf) given time — separation also minimizes interface.

findings.summary:
CORRECTION to this study's own acceptance wording: fractional length starts at ~0.5 at
labelling (raw), not ~1.0. A random 50/50 label makes ~half of all interfaces heterotypic.
The paper's curves start at 1.0 only because they are NORMALIZED by the t=0 value.

question:
Can we build Chaste plus the authors' CellBasedComparison2017 project from source and
regenerate the cell-sorting output of Osborne et al. 2017 — producing per-model
heterotypicboundary.dat trajectories that serve as the ground truth for every later study?
hypothesis:
The project builds against modern mainline Chaste (its copyright headers run to 2021 and its
CI claims continuous testing), and once the paper-parameter blocks are restored the five
sorting sims reproduce Fig 2 qualitatively — CA, CP and VM reaching engulfment; OS and VT
stalling at a local minimum.
objective:
Build Chaste + CellBasedComparison2017, restore the paper parameters that the repo ships
commented out, run TestCellSortingLiteratePaper for all five models across 10 seeds, and
archive the resulting heterotypicboundary.dat files as the investigation's reference dataset.
description:
This study exists because the expert asked for a careful comparison against existing Chaste
results, and chose regenerated C++ output over published figures as the reference.

The critical trap is documented in the authors' own source: every test file ships with the
paper parameters COMMENTED OUT and short continuous-integration values active. For cell
sorting, M_TIME_FOR_SIMULATION is 11.0 in the repo versus 100 in the paper. Running the
suite as-cloned produces a plausible-looking but wrong baseline — the single highest-risk
silent failure in this investigation. Restoring those blocks is step one, and the diff must
be recorded.

The build is the other risk. The project's CMakeLists declares
find_package(Chaste COMPONENTS cell_based crypt), so the crypt component must be built even
though the sorting case study does not use it. The paper pins historical Chaste branches
(paper/CellBasedComparison, paper/CellBasedComparison18) against Oxford servers that are no
longer the live mirror; we build against the GitHub mirror's develop and record the commit.

Output lands in $CHASTE_TEST_OUTPUT/CellSorting/{Ca,Potts,Node,Mesh,Vertex}. The measure the
investigation turns on is heterotypicboundary.dat, whose four columns are
(heterotypic_boundary_length, total_shared_edges_length, num_heterotypic_pairs,
total_num_pairs). The paper's fractional boundary length is column 1 / column 2 — the writer
does NOT divide, so the reduction is ours to perform and to test.

expected_behavior.en: Fractional boundary length declines from its post-labelling value as cells sort.

expected_behavior.name: cxx-interface-more-than-halves
expected_behavior.en: By t=110 the heterotypic interface is well below its post-labelling value (sorting occurred).

reproducibility_metrics.tutorial_source:
Our own build of Chaste/CellBasedComparison2017 against chaste/release, compared to the
PUBLISHED paper (Osborne et al. 2017, Fig 3, k_pert=1). This study reproduces the tutorial
itself; it is the reference that cbc-04 then reproduces in PyChaste.
reproducibility_metrics.comparison:
Fractional boundary length normalized by its value at labelling (t=10), as Fig 3 plots it.
Paper values are read approximately off Fig 3-left (black curves) — the paper ships curves,
not tables, so tutorial_value here is an eyeballed plateau, not an exact figure.

metrics.note: Approx. from Fig 3; OS sorts most (fully separates).
VT stalls highest, matching the paper's 'OS/VT differ from CA/CP/VM' claim.

qualitative.detail: Model ordering (VT > VM > CA > CP > OS by residual interface) matches Fig 3.

caveats: Tutorial values are read off the published figure, not exact — this study's role is to establish OUR C++ run as the exact reference for cbc-04, which is compared numerically.
Single seed (0). The tutorial itself is single-run; the paper's curves are 10-seed means.

baseline.name: cp-sorting
baseline.description: Cellular Potts sorting (OnLatticeSimulation + Potts update rules).

baseline.name: vm-sorting
baseline.description: Vertex sorting (Nagai-Honda differential adhesion + diffusion noise).

cxx-fractional-length-declines.detail: All five models' fractional length declines from the post-labelling value (reduction via sorting_analysis); normalized endpoints OS 0.08, CP 0.19, CA 0.50, VM 0.55, VT 0.91.

cxx-interface-more-than-halves.detail: Every model ends below its post-labelling value (ratio_at_most 1.0): CP/OS/CA/VM drop substantially; VT declines least (0.485->0.440).

prep_findings.summary: The cell-sorting paper-parameter restoration is a SINGLE line, confirmed against the clone.
prep_findings.evidence:
test/TestCellSortingLiteratePaper.hpp line 81: `M_TIME_FOR_SIMULATION = 11.0` (CI value)
must become 100 (paper value; the commented-out paper block at lines 75-78 confirms 100).
M_TIME_TO_STEADY_STATE (10) and M_NUM_CELLS_ACROSS (20) are ALREADY at paper values in the
active block, so no other edit is needed for this case study. M_CELL_FLUCTUATION stays 1.0
(it is the k_pert knob; 1.0 is the Fig 2 baseline).

prep_findings.summary: Build host chosen: the Mac mini (2.5 TiB free, Docker 29.5.2), against chaste/release.

notes:
DECIDED: builds/runs on the Mac mini (per the expert). The pbg-chaste branch is synced there
and the chaste/release image (prebuilt Chaste C++, ~24 GB) is being pulled. The project's
CMake declares COMPONENTS cell_based crypt, so the crypt component must be available in the
image even though the sorting case study does not use it — to be confirmed when the image
layout is inspected. Both mini and laptop are Apple Silicon, so runs are emulated regardless;
the mini's value is being persistent and out of the laptop's way.
